summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout CGM were 98.7 percent complete, with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, time below range 5.1 percent, and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent. Local-hour lows clustered at 01:00 (time below range 18.5 percent) and 19:00 (15.3 percent), while 14:00-16:00 local had the most time above range. The selected AAPS profile is complete and declared historically applicable. Zero carb entries were present, so always-on SMB with UAM and Dynamic ISF at 70 percent supplied most meal-time insulin. Overnight lows can still be residual IOB with a 10 h DIA, the 90 mg/dL overnight target, or 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h; those explanations are not separated, so every inventory value is kept and the next step is observation rather than a setting edit.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM quality is good: 3995 valid entries, 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, no invalids or duplicates. Edge days 7 Aug and 21 Aug are partial. The selected aaps_profile is complete. Carb telemetry is empty (0 g, 0 carb treatments). Only representative treatments and loop snapshots are supplied. A 13 Aug profile-switch note names u200 dilute basal 16-2u per day FLAT ISF; profile_context still declares historical applicability yes, so the selected profile is not treated as absent. Site changes, sensor changes, 19 Aug occlusion and pump error, and GLP-1 1.25 mg notes limit causal attribution.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality status good; glucose_summary entry_count 3995; treatment_summary carb_entries 0 and total_carbs_g 0.0; carb_treatment_entries empty; representative_events include the 13 Aug profile switch, 19 Aug occlusion, and GLP-1 notes; profile_context historical_applicability yes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Full treatment and SMB time series, activity notes, dilution factor, free_peak peak time, and pre-switch numeric profile values are not in the package.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range 5.1 percent and CV 32.6 percent are the binding safety limits, not time in range. Local danger hours are 00:00-03:00 and 19:00. Extremes include 41-42 mg/dL on 13, 14, and 21 Aug and 290-293 mg/dL on 15 and 18 Aug. Sampled IOB at highs reached about 4.7-5.9 U. Labeled corrections are usually 0.05-0.35 U, so loop SMB, UAM, and temp basal dominate insulin. Overnight mean glucose sits near the 90 mg/dL target while time below range is already double-digit. No insulin-up overnight and no afternoon insulin-up justified by time above range alone.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary TBR 5.1 percent and CV 32.6 percent; hourly_glucose_local hour 1 TBR 18.5 percent and hour 19 TBR 15.3 percent; glucose_extremes; representative_loop_statuses with IOB 4.73 U and 5.935 U; therapy_response_windows with large swings after tiny labeled boluses.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality: empty COB, long DIA, device events, and declared profile applicability.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Hypo rescue carbs, overnight IOB at 00:00 each night, activity after 16:00 local, and a complete SMB timeline around each extreme.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight 00:00-03:00 local is not a clean fasting test because DIA is 10 h. Means near 90-93 mg/dL with high TBR can reflect 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h, leftover IOB, overnight SMB toward 90 mg/dL, or the target itself. Hours 06:00-08:00 local are the most stable (TIR about 98-99 percent), so 06:00 basal 0.8 U/h is not shown to be too low. The 09:00-17:00 climb and 16:00 TAR 32.1 percent occur with COB 0 and active UAM, so 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h is not a proven under-basal defect and may be protective before 19:00 lows. Target 100 mg/dL from 08:00 is not the main daytime-high explanation. Target returns to 90 mg/dL at 23:00 while evening TBR is already elevated.
analysis_steps.evidence: basal_segments 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.7/0.5/0.6/0.7 U/h; target_segments 90 then 100 then 90 mg/dL; hourly_glucose_local; many zero-rate temp basals and high temps in representative_treatments; afternoon temporary targets of 135 mg/dL in representative_events.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview TBR constraint; data_quality empty carbs and 10 h DIA.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True low-IOB fasting nights, IOB at local midnight, and whether 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h was already chosen after prior evening lows.

analysis_steps.findings: Five CR segments exist but had no carb stream, so CR was unused rather than missing. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is not the live ISF: Dynamic ISF is on at 70 percent and snapshot variable_sens ranged from about 28 to 124 mg/dL/U. DIA 10 h can carry afternoon UAM or DynISF IOB into 00:00-03:00. Correction windows are not clean ISF tests because SMB, temp basal, unlogged intake, and the 19 Aug occlusion coexist. CR, ISF, and DIA cannot be edited as independent numbers while automation dominates.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_ratio_segments 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, 12.6 g/U; isf_segments 56 mg/dL/U; dia_hours 10.0; loop variable_sens and COB 0; therapy_response_windows all Correction Bolus with is_extended_carbs false.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets unresolved overnight cause; safety_overview TBR; later automation stages.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Logged meals, whether the bolus wizard is used at all, DynISF TDD method, and u200 dilution factor.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and match the unlogged-meal workflow. Activation flags are internally consistent: always-on SMB, COB and after-carbs SMB off, SMB with temp target on, SMB with high temp target off. Interval 3 min can stack insulin quickly on a 10 h DIA. Configured 15/20 min SMB caps imply small doses from 0.5-0.8 U/h basal, but sampled reasons include microboluses of 0.3-0.4 U and a UAM high-boost SMB of 1.6 U after the 19 Aug occlusion, so a custom boost path can exceed naive basal-minutes math. UAM is the meal engine, not duplicate COB counting. Remaining low-temp wait time is not the configured interval.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled true; uam_enabled true; smb_always_enabled true; smb_interval_minutes 3; max_smb_basal_minutes 15; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes 20; loop reasons with COB 0, Enhanced oref1, UAM Boost, and UAM High Boost; hourly afternoon TAR then 19:00 TBR.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview; basal_targets (afternoon TAR is not a basal proof); profile_cr_isf_dia (CR idle, DIA 10 h).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete SMB timestamps and whether always-on SMB overrides a 135 mg/dL high temp target on this build.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is false and Autosens target raise/lower are false, which is consistent. A snapshot sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not proof that sensitivity is unused; other snapshots show ratios down to 0.79 and Dynamic ISF is the live ISF. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U are far above observed delivery (about 4 U/h maxSafeBasal and peak sampled IOB about 5.9 U), so those caps are oversized but not the TBR mechanism. Carb-absorption settings had no COB to validate. Enabling Autosens on top of Dynamic ISF would be a dual change and is withheld.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled false; dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent 70 percent; max_basal_u_per_hour 12; max_iob_units 25; loop variable_sens 27.8-124 and maxSafeBasal about 4 U/h; min_5m_carbimpact 8; meal_max_absorption_hours 7.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview; profile_cr_isf_dia; automation_smb_uam. Competing levers are SMB interval 3 min, DynISF 70 percent, and overnight target 90 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: DynISF TDD calculation method and a controlled period with one automation lever held constant.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared analysis_context has meal_strategies empty and strategy_stable_for_period null. There are no non-null prebolus_minutes or immediate_bolus_percent fields to reproduce. Observed execution matches that empty declaration: no meal boluses, only correction windows, COB 0, and UAM or SMB covering afternoon rises. Prebolus minutes and immediate bolus percent must not be invented. Afternoon TAR then 18:00-19:00 TBR is the recurring meal-linked safety pattern and is tied to automation IOB plus DIA 10 h, not to a CR number.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.analysis_context meal_strategies empty; treatment_summary carb_entries 0; therapy_response_windows event_type Correction Bolus only; hourly_glucose_local 12:00-19:00; GLP-1 notes on 14, 17, and 20 Aug.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carb grams and clock time for afternoon events, and whether any insulin was given before the first rise.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amount, start offset, or duration is declared, and extended_carb_entries is 0. E-carbs are not inferred from temp basal, SMB streams, or any aggregate duration. Carb-absorption model settings are idle. Adding e-carbs without real carb entries would create a second carb path on top of UAM and is not supported.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries 0; average_extended_carb_duration_min null; carb_treatment_entries empty; all response windows is_extended_carbs false.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None for current unused status. Meal-linked carb amounts would be required before any e-carb duration review.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked causes: (1) unlogged daytime intake covered late by UAM and Dynamic ISF, leaving IOB that can explain 19:00 and 00:00-03:00 lows via DIA 10 h; (2) overnight target 90 mg/dL sitting on the hypo line and allowing overnight SMB; (3) unproven 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h contribution. Rejected as first fixes: raising 16:00 basal or tightening CR because of afternoon TAR; cutting max basal 12 U/h or max IOB 25 U as the TBR mechanism; editing idle carb-absorption settings. Contradiction audit: profile_context historical_applicability yes overrides any earlier suggestion that the selected profile was absent before 13 Aug; empty meal_strategies is a declared empty plan, not a missing non-null field; live ISF is Dynamic ISF, not 56 mg/dL/U. Because those overnight explanations remain entangled, every inventory item is keep. Safe order is profile observation first, then at most one automation lever, then meal logging before any CR or e-carb work.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined hourly_glucose_local poles; empty carb telemetry versus enabled UAM; DynISF variable_sens versus flat ISF 56; decision_inventory complete current values; analysis_context recent_results empty.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The single most useful missing observation is local 00:00 IOB paired with the same night 00:00-03:00 time below range after a lower-insulin afternoon.

strengths: CGM coverage 98.7 percent is adequate for hourly pattern review.
Overall time in range 86.0 percent with daytime morning hours 06:00-08:00 local near 98-99 percent time in range.
The selected profile object is complete, including basal, CR, ISF, target, DIA, and SMB settings.
User already used raised temporary targets around some afternoon rises.
Always-on SMB with UAM is internally consistent with zero logged carbs.
issues: Time below range 5.1 percent with local clusters at 01:00 (18.5 percent) and 19:00 (15.3 percent).
Coefficient of variation 32.6 percent with afternoon time above range peaking at 32.1 percent at 16:00 local.
No carb entries, so meal insulin cannot be separated from basal, UAM, Dynamic ISF, temporary targets, or corrections.
Overnight mean glucose sits near the 90 mg/dL target, so target, residual IOB, and 00:00 basal remain competing explanations.
Occlusion and pump error on 19 Aug, GLP-1 notes, a u200 dilute profile name, and a 13 Aug profile-switch note confound some high and low extremes.

recommendations.title: Keep the overnight profile and compare midnight IOB with overnight lows
recommendations.description: Local 00:00-03:00 time below range occurs while mean glucose is already near 90 mg/dL, but afternoon UAM and Dynamic ISF IOB plus a 10 h DIA can still be active. That does not isolate target 90 mg/dL from 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h. The first safe action is to keep overnight target and basal unchanged and record IOB at local 00:00 versus the same night overnight time below range.

suggested_change.next_observation: local 00:00 IOB and 00:00-03:00 time below range

recommendations.title: Do not raise afternoon basal because of time above range
recommendations.description: Hour 16 local time above range 32.1 percent occurred with COB 0, UAM enabled, and later 19:00 time below range 15.3 percent. Raising 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h would stack on meal-time automation and is not supported as a first step.

recommendations.title: Review at most one automation lever after the overnight IOB check
recommendations.description: SMB interval 3 min and Dynamic ISF 70 percent can both explain late stacking. They must not be changed together, and neither should be changed in the same step as basal, ISF, CR, or target. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U were not the observed ceiling.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the selected profile unchanged, including overnight target 90 mg/dL and 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight time below range is the binding pattern, but package data do not separate leftover afternoon IOB on a 10 h DIA from the 90 mg/dL target or from 00:00 basal. Afternoon time above range is explained at least as well by unlogged intake plus UAM and Dynamic ISF. No profile segment therefore has an isolated, supported old-to-new value.
profile_recommendation.next_check: For several nights, record IOB at local 00:00 and whether 00:00-03:00 time below range still occurs after afternoons with low IOB and no large UAM or SMB stack.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local 00:00-03:00 time below range with mean glucose near 90 mg/dL. Uncertainty: DIA 10 h and afternoon UAM IOB can still be active, so this is not a clean fasting basal test. Dependencies: overnight target 90 mg/dL and Dynamic ISF or SMB stacking. A downward change is not isolated and an upward change is unsafe while time below range is binding.

Evidence: local hour 5 mean 104.2 mg/dL with time below range 4.8 percent and no clear dawn rise. Uncertainty: transition hour with possible residual night IOB. Dependencies: 00:00 and 06:00 segments. No isolated defect.

Evidence: local 06:00-08:00 time in range about 97.5-98.7 percent with almost no time below range except one 21 Aug extreme. Uncertainty: later 09:00-10:00 rise looks meal or UAM shaped. Dependencies: 08:00 target 100 mg/dL and unlogged intake. Not shown as too low or too high.

Evidence: late-morning and midday climb with COB 0. Uncertainty: UAM, corrections, and possible meals dominate this window. Dependencies: SMB or UAM and Dynamic ISF. Daytime basal cannot be blamed or raised on this pattern.

Evidence: hour 16 local has the highest time above range (32.1 percent) but hour 19 has time below range 15.3 percent. Uncertainty: the 0.5 U/h step may already be anti-hypo design. Dependencies: UAM or SMB IOB and 19:00 basal 0.7 U/h. Raising this segment is unsupported.

Evidence: local 18:00-19:00 falling glucose and rising time below range. Uncertainty: this is more consistent with prior afternoon insulin than with a unique 18:00 basal error. Dependencies: 16:00 basal, UAM stack, and DIA 10 h.

Evidence: basal steps up from 0.5 to 0.7 U/h into the highest evening time-below-range hour. Uncertainty: timing may matter, but leftover UAM IOB is an equally plausible cause. Dependencies: afternoon automation and overnight target. Not isolated enough to change.

Evidence: zero carb entries and sampled COB 0, so this CR did not drive insulin. Uncertainty: overnight lows are IOB, target, or basal questions, not a carb-ratio test. Dependencies: unused meal logging. Changing CR would be speculative.
Evidence: no carb treatments in this or any segment. Uncertainty: cannot validate a tighter predawn CR. Dependencies: empty declared meal strategy and UAM workflow.

Evidence: morning rise after 08:00 is compatible with unlogged intake covered by UAM, not a measured CR miss. Uncertainty: no carb grams or bolus percent. Dependencies: SMB or UAM activation with COB-based SMB off.

Evidence: afternoon is the main high window, but CR is unused when carbs are not entered. Uncertainty: a tighter CR cannot be blamed for UAM-only dosing. Dependencies: UAM, Dynamic ISF, and evening time below range. Do not tighten CR to chase hour-16 highs.
Evidence: evening pattern is falling glucose and time below range, not an unused CR failure. Uncertainty: no evening carb log. Dependencies: DIA 10 h and afternoon IOB.

Evidence: flat profile ISF 56 is overridden by Dynamic ISF, with variable_sens about 28-124 mg/dL/U in snapshots. Uncertainty: correction windows mix SMB, temp basal, unlogged intake, and occlusion. Dependencies: aaps.core.sensitivity. Editing 56 would not be identifiable while Dynamic ISF remains on.

Evidence: overnight mean sits on 90 mg/dL with high time below range, so the target is a plausible contributor and a candidate later single lever. Uncertainty: residual IOB and 00:00 basal are not ruled out. Dependencies: profile.target.23_00, profile.basal.00_00, SMB toward 90 mg/dL, and DIA 10 h. A change is withheld until midnight IOB is observed.

Evidence: 06:00-08:00 control is strong and later highs occur well above 100 mg/dL with COB 0. Uncertainty: temporary targets of 135 mg/dL were also used some afternoons. Dependencies: UAM and Dynamic ISF, not this daytime target. No isolated target defect.

Evidence: target returns to 90 mg/dL at 23:00 while hour 23 local already has time below range 10.1 percent. Uncertainty: this is the same overnight-target question as 00:00, not a separate proven error. Dependencies: profile.target.00_00 and leftover IOB. Keep both overnight target rows together rather than editing one.

Evidence: 10 h DIA is a credible bridge from afternoon IOB to overnight time below range. Uncertainty: free_peak_oref peak time and u200 dilution are unknown, so a shorter DIA is not validated. Dependencies: UAM or SMB dose timing. Do not shorten DIA in the same step as any insulin-delivery change.

Evidence: zero carbs and COB 0 mean UAM is the meal insulin path, not duplicate COB counting. Uncertainty: UAM timing likely contributes to evening lows. Dependencies: empty meal declaration and idle CR. Disabling SMB or UAM without a carb-logging alternative is unsupported. No source component is null, so verify is not used.

Evidence: flags match an unlogged-meal setup. Uncertainty: whether always-on SMB overrides a 135 mg/dL high temp target on this build. Dependencies: observed afternoon temporary targets. The set is consistent and has no null component.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: observed rates were limited near 4 U/h maxSafeBasal and peak sampled IOB about 5.9 U, so 12 U/h and 25 U did not create the time-below-range pattern. Uncertainty: the caps would not stop a future stack. Dependencies: safety multipliers, not profile basal. Tightening them is not the first action and must not be paired with basal or SMB edits.

Evidence: Dynamic ISF is the live ISF and can treat unlogged rises as resistance, then over-correct. Autosens off is consistent with Autosens target flags. Uncertainty: 70 percent versus SMB interval 3 min. Dependencies: flat ISF 56, UAM, and DIA 10 h. Do not enable Autosens on top of Dynamic ISF, and do not change 70 percent in the same step as SMB delivery or profile ISF.

Evidence: no carb or e-carb entries, so min_5m_carbimpact and 7 h absorption did not drive COB or SMB. Uncertainty: unused settings cannot be validated. Dependencies: meal logging. Leave unchanged until carbs are entered.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Treat meals as unannounced: no declared prebolus minutes and no declared immediate bolus percent, so invent neither; keep SMB and UAM as the meal insulin; do not add e-carbs while COB is unused. Prioritize avoiding extra afternoon insulin that can still act at 19:00 and overnight because DIA is 10 h.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared analysis_context.meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Telemetry matches that declaration with 0 g carbs, no e-carb durations, and all response windows labeled Correction Bolus. The recurring harm is late automation IOB after afternoon rises, not a measured missed prebolus.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carb grams and clock time for a few afternoon rises and note whether any insulin was given before the first rise.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring local 12:00-17:00 rise then 18:00-19:00 fall, sometimes with a 135 mg/dL temporary target
exceptions.suggestion: Stay in the same unannounced UAM frame and do not add CR edits, e-carbs, or extra manual correction in that same window
exceptions.rationale: That couplet is already explained by UAM or Dynamic ISF IOB plus long DIA and is not a second meal recipe

implementation_steps: Confirm independently that the selected aaps_profile is the pump profile in use and that CGM gaps around extremes are understood before any discussion of settings.
Keep every current profile segment unchanged and first record local 00:00 IOB against the same night 00:00-03:00 time below range, especially after lower-insulin afternoons.
Do not raise afternoon basal or change any CR segment while carbs remain unlogged and UAM is covering rises.
Only after that overnight check, consider reviewing one automation lever at most: either SMB interval or Dynamic ISF percent, never both, and never in the same step as basal, ISF, CR, DIA, or target.
If meal work is next, start with carb logging rather than e-carbs, prebolus minutes, or an invented immediate bolus percent.
If any single setting is later changed, change only that item, monitor glucose closely, and reassess evening and overnight time below range before another edit.
education: Time in range can look strong while time below range and variability still limit how aggressively overnight target or daytime automation can be interpreted.
When no carbs are logged, UAM estimates unannounced glucose rises; that is not the same as COB counting the same meal twice.
Dynamic ISF can move live sensitivity far from a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, so highs and crashes can both appear even if the clock ISF number is unchanged.
A 10 h DIA means afternoon SMB or UAM can still be insulin on board at midnight, which mimics overnight over-basal.
E-carbs are a carb-absorption announcement, not a pump extended bolus, and they cannot be inferred from temp basal or SMB history.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely. TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
Time below range 5.1 percent, including readings of 41-42 mg/dL, is the binding constraint on any later insulin-up idea.
The profile name refers to u200 dilute insulin; displayed units may not match U100 rules of thumb.
The 19 Aug occlusion and pump error can explain part of that day's hyperglycemia and later catch-up IOB.
Discuss any future single-lever idea with the care team before changing AAPS. Do not change AAPS automatically.
